newsitem.title: USA: S3 buys stake in Faroudja Laboratories.
newsitem.headline: S3 buys stake in Faroudja Laboratories.

text.p: S3 Inc on Wednesday said it bought a stake in video equipment maker Faroudja Laboratories for an undisclosed sum.

S3 said it would use Faroudja's expertise to bring cinematic-quality video to personal computers. The companies will work together to develop computer chips that would allow viewers to watch movies and television broadcasts through PC monitors.
PC monitors can display images much more clearly than regular television sets. But they lose their clarity when displaying TV signals because of format incompatibilities.
Faroudja, a closely held maker of home-theater equipment, has come up with several ways to sharpen the resolution of ordinary TV signals.

S3, which specializes in making graphics chips for PCs, will license Faroudja's technology and develop chips around it. The chips will enable PCs to display high-quality video from digital television broadcasters, satellite TV services or digital versatile disk, or DVD, players, the companies said.

The licensing agreement is part of S3's strategy to pursue the emerging market for devices that merge the power of the personal computer with the television set, said Gary Johnson, chief executive of S3.
"We're going to bring the home-theater experience to the PC," Johnson said.
Shares of S3, based in Santa Clara, Calif., jumped 1-3/8, or about 13 percent, to 12-7/8 in early afternoon trading on the Nasdaq.
